diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Although most subset selection criteria are NP hard,
not all are. For example, a submatrix $\mc$ with minimal Frobenius norm can be computed
in polynomial time

Unfortunately, creating such a gap is not always feasible~\cite[Section 1]{Papa1991}, and we were
 not able to do so for a few criteria, including
 Schatten 
 $p$-norm minimization for $p>2$

issues.failure_explanation: Read collectively, the abstract promises NP-hardness and PTAS-inapproximability for every listed criterion. The paper explicitly says that Frobenius column-norm minimization is polynomial-time solvable and that no PTAS-excluding gap was obtained for Schatten p-norm minimization or p-norm condition-number minimization.

failure_location.quote:
We show that these criteria 
are NP hard and do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract to say that most criteria are NP-hard and only the explicitly proved subset lacks a PTAS, and list the exceptions.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract materially overstates both the complexity classifications and the set of criteria proved not to admit a PTAS.
issues.title: Abstract overstates the NP-hardness and PTAS-inapproximability coverage
issues.why_classification: A local wording correction restores agreement with the formal results and sacrifices none of the paper's proved guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where inputs are rational numbers and the input size is measured in the number of bits.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's declared bit model, a polynomial-time reduction must output a matrix with rational, bit-representable entries. The entry 1/sqrt(3) is irrational, so the constructed matrix is not a valid input to the stated decision problems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the construction by a rational unit-norm incidence construction, for example support entries 1/2 together with a unique rational dummy coordinate 1/2 for each column, and recompute all singular values and thresholds.
issues.overall_effect: Every NP-hardness and inapproximability theorem based on this exact construction is unestablished in the paper's stated computational model.
issues.title: The X3C reduction uses irrational entries despite the rational-input Turing model
issues.why_classification: The advertised classifications can plausibly all be retained, but the repair requires a new global reduction construction and a recalculation of the constants rather than a purely local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
In the reduced instance we set
$m = 3M$, $k=M$, and $b=1$.
\emph{Instance:} Matrix $\ma \in \real^{m\times n}$ with $\rank(\ma) \geq k$ and unit-norm columns

issues.failure_explanation: The stated X3C instances are not restricted to M at least 2 or n at least M. If M=1 and no K_i equals S, the X3C instance is false, yet every single nonzero column is orthonormal, so the claimed equivalence is true on the matrix side. If n<M, the constructed matrix has fewer than k columns and cannot satisfy the decision instance's rank requirement.

failure_location.quote: the instance of X3C is true if and only if there exists a submatrix $\mc_*\in \mathbb{R}^{(3M)\times M}$ with orthonormal columns.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Preprocess the trivial X3C instances or restrict the reduction to M at least 2 and n at least M, mapping the excluded instances to fixed correct yes or no instances.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the reduction is not correct or not defined on all instances permitted by its own X3C formulation, so the downstream reductions inherit the gap.
issues.title: The X3C reduction omits necessary degenerate-instance side conditions
issues.why_classification: Adding and preprocessing standard boundary conditions is a local repair that preserves the reduction, constants, and advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The decision problems: volume maximization and S-optimality maximization are NP hard.
A decision problem is \textit{NP complete} if it is in NP and it is also NP hard.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose upgrades the theorem's NP-hardness conclusion to NP-completeness. Under the paper's own definition, that additionally requires membership in NP, but no certificate or polynomial-time verification argument is given.

failure_location.quote:
We show that volume
and S-optimality maximization are NP complete (Section~\ref{s_volume1})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add a membership-in-NP verification argument for the two decision problems or change the prose to NP-hard.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity classification stated in the section overview is stronger than the formal theorem establishes.
issues.title: NP-completeness is asserted for volume and S-optimality without proving membership in NP
issues.why_classification: The mismatch can be removed by a short standard membership proof or a local weakening of the prose, with no loss to the paper's main hardness results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.
Assume that X3C instance is false, and assume that any two columns of~$\mc$ overlap.

issues.failure_explanation: A false X3C instance guarantees one overlapping pair in a selected M-column family, not that every pair or every (k-1)-column prefix overlaps. For example, one may select two overlapping sets and a third set disjoint from both; a two-column prefix consisting of disjoint sets has volume 1, two-norm 1, and pseudo-inverse norms below the asserted induction thresholds. The same unjustified induction or explicit all-pairs assumption is reused in the two-norm, pseudo-inverse, and related threshold proofs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Order the columns so that an overlapping pair comes first, then append the remaining columns and apply the corrected block-volume estimate, singular-value interlacing, or Lemma l_fi as appropriate; handle rank-deficient selections separately.
issues.overall_effect: The stated false-instance bounds for volume, norms, pseudo-inverse norms, condition numbers, and stable rank are unsupported as written, together with results derived from those bounds.
issues.title: The inductions incorrectly treat every column prefix as though it contained an overlap
issues.why_classification: A local reordering argument using tools already in the paper preserves the numerical bounds and requires no new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
for each $\epsilon>0$
 there exists a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for minimization problems, and a $(1-\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for maximization problems

It is NP hard to approximate Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of 
$\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

issues.failure_explanation: The factors (2sqrt(2)/3)^(1/k) and sqrt(1+1/(4k)) tend to 1 as k grows. To exclude a PTAS, one must exhibit a fixed epsilon_0>0 for which (1-epsilon_0)- or (1+epsilon_0)-approximation is NP-hard. Hardness only at an input-dependent accuracy approaching exactness does not contradict a PTAS at any fixed looser accuracy.

failure_location.quote:
It is NP hard to approximate S-optimality maximization within a factor of 
$(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$. Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either withdraw these no-PTAS conclusions or provide a new NP-hardness reduction with a multiplicative gap bounded away from 1 by a constant independent of k.
issues.overall_effect: The no-PTAS conclusions for S-optimality, Frobenius and Schatten p-norm pseudo-inverse minimization, and Frobenius condition-number minimization are not established.
issues.title: Approximation gaps tending to one do not rule out a PTAS
issues.why_classification: Retaining the advertised no-PTAS guarantees requires a fundamentally new constant-gap hardness argument; otherwise a central guarantee of each affected theorem is abandoned.

issues.failure_explanation: From sigma_1(C) at least 1, one obtains k/sigma_1(C)^p at most k, not at least k. Thus the displayed second inequality goes in the wrong direction and does not prove the stated lower bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the lemma's later nonnegative function g(x)=x^2+2/(px^p)-(1+2/p): summing it over all singular values directly yields ||C^dagger||_(p)^p at least k.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal Schatten p-norm value k^(1/p), and consequently the p-norm pseudo-inverse decision and threshold arguments that use it, lack a valid proof as written.
issues.title: The Schatten p-norm pseudo-inverse lower bound reverses an inequality
issues.why_classification: A short rearrangement of an inequality already present in the same proof repairs the bound and preserves every downstream claim.

issues.failure_explanation: For positive blocks A and B, the Schatten q-norm of diag(A,B) is (||A||_q^q+||B||_q^q)^(1/q), not ||A||_q+||B||_q. The claimed conclusion is false: for C=I_2 partitioned into its two columns and p=4, the left side is ||I_2||_(4)^2=sqrt(2), while the right side is 1+1=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conclusion with the bound supplied by pinching, ||C^dagger||_(p)^2 at least (||C_1^dagger||_(p)^p+||C_2^dagger||_(p)^p)^(2/p).
issues.overall_effect: The stated p-norm lower bound for partitioned pseudo-inverses is invalid for every p>2.
issues.title: The pinching argument falsely replaces a block-diagonal Schatten norm by a sum
issues.why_classification: A contained corrected pinching statement survives, but the original sum-of-squares guarantee must be materially weakened.
